risk_modules.title: Heart Disease (WHO South Asia 10-Year CVD Risk)
risk_modules.methodology: Continuous South-Asia-calibrated 10-year cardiovascular & stroke risk model (ages 40–74) using lab-based total cholesterol or non-lab BMI.
risk_modules.why_it_matters: South Asians experience coronary artery disease and stroke roughly 5–10 years earlier than global averages, often with modest LDL cholesterol.

thresholds.skipped: Outside ages 40–74 (displays modifiable risk-factor count instead of guessed %)

recommended_tests: Fasting Lipid Profile (Total Chol, LDL, HDL, TG)
red_flags: Chest pain/pressure radiating to arm or jaw

risk_modules.title: BMI & Central Obesity (Indian Consensus Cutoffs)
risk_modules.methodology: Indian Consensus BMI (<18.5 underweight, 18.5–22.9 normal, 23.0–24.9 overweight, >=25.0 obese) paired with waist circumference (>=90 cm men, >=80 cm women).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Indians accumulate higher visceral/abdominal fat at lower BMI ('thin-fat' phenotype), driving insulin resistance even when BMI looks borderline.

thresholds.low: BMI 18.5–22.9 kg/m² AND waist <90 cm (M) / <80 cm (F)
thresholds.high: BMI >= 25.0 kg/m² (obese) OR central obesity (waist >=90 cm M / >=80 cm F)

recommended_tests: Liver ultrasound / ALT if central obesity present
red_flags: Rapid unexplained weight gain with leg swelling or breathlessness (possible fluid retention)

risk_modules.title: Metabolic Syndrome (Harmonized South Asian Criteria)
risk_modules.methodology: Counts 5 cardiometabolic criteria: elevated waist (>=90M/80F), BP >=130/85, FPG >=100 mg/dL, Triglycerides >=150 mg/dL, low HDL (<40M/50F).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Meeting >=3 of 5 criteria doubles 10-year cardiovascular risk and strongly predicts type 2 diabetes and fatty liver (MASLD).

thresholds.skipped: Skipped when fasting glucose, triglycerides, and HDL are all missing (never guessed)

red_flags: Co-existing chest discomfort, severe fatigue, or persistent hypertension >=180/120

risk_modules.title: Diabetes Risk (MDRF Indian Diabetes Risk Score)
risk_modules.methodology: Validated Indian screening score (0–100) combining age, waist circumference, physical activity, and parental diabetes history.
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Over 50% of Indians with early type 2 diabetes are asymptomatic; IDRS identifies high-risk individuals before complications begin.
modifiable_drivers: Daily physical activity (30–45 min brisk walking)
red_flags: Extreme thirst/urination with nausea, confusion, or glucose >400 / <54 mg/dL

risk_modules.title: Blood Pressure (ACC/AHA & Indian Hypertension Staging)
risk_modules.methodology: Stages systolic/diastolic BP into Normal (<120/80), Elevated (120–129/<80), Stage 1 (130–139 or 80–89), Stage 2 (>=140 or >=90), Crisis (>=180 or >=120).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: High blood pressure is the #1 modifiable driver of stroke, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease in India.

thresholds.high: Stage 2 (>=140 / >=90 mmHg) or Hypertensive Crisis (>=180 / >=120 mmHg)
thresholds.skipped: Requires positive systolic and diastolic BP

modifiable_drivers: Dietary sodium (<5 g salt/day; cut pickles & papad)
recommended_tests: Home BP log (morning & evening for 7 days)
red_flags: BP >=180/120 with headache, vision changes, chest pain, or weakness -> Call 112/108

risk_modules.title: Kidney Health (CKD-EPI 2021 Race-Free eGFR + Urine ACR)
risk_modules.methodology: KDIGO-aligned CKD-EPI 2021 race-free filtration equation (G1 >=90 to G5 <15 mL/min/1.73m²) combined with Urine ACR albuminuria staging (A1–A3).
risk_modules.why_it_matters: Diabetic and hypertensive kidney damage is silent until advanced; catching eGFR <60 or ACR >=30 early allows kidney-protective therapy.

thresholds.low: eGFR >= 60 mL/min/1.73m² AND Urine ACR < 30 mg/g (if tested)
thresholds.skipped: Requires serum creatinine lab value (never guessed)

red_flags: Sudden drop in urine output, severe leg/facial swelling, or breathlessness

faqs.title: Why South Asian BMI and waist cutoffs are stricter
faqs.summary: Indian consensus uses BMI >=23 for overweight and >=25 for obesity (instead of 25/30) because South Asians carry higher visceral fat at lower body weights.
faqs.answer: Indian Consensus Guidelines (Misra et al.) define BMI 18.5-22.9 kg/m2 as normal, 23.0-24.9 as overweight, and >=25.0 as obese. Central obesity is flagged at waist >=90 cm for men and >=80 cm for women because abdominal visceral fat drives insulin resistance, fatty liver, and early cardiovascular risk even at modest BMI.

faqs.title: Understanding CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR and Urine ACR
faqs.summary: CKD-EPI 2021 estimates kidney filtration without race adjustment; pairing eGFR with Urine ACR catches early diabetic or hypertensive kidney strain.
faqs.answer: Kidney risk uses both eGFR (G1 >=90, G2 60-89, G3a 45-59, G3b 30-44, G4 15-29, G5 <15 mL/min/1.73m2) and Urine ACR (A1 <30, A2 30-300, A3 >300 mg/g). Even with eGFR >=90, an ACR >=30 mg/g indicates early kidney stress that responds well to BP and sugar control.

faqs.title: How brisk walking lowers blood sugar and BP
faqs.summary: 30 minutes of brisk walking daily improves insulin uptake for up to 24 hours and lowers systolic BP by 4-8 mmHg.
faqs.answer: Walking recruits large leg muscles that absorb glucose even with lower insulin levels. Aim for 30-45 minutes on 5+ days/week at a pace where you can talk in short sentences without gasping.

faqs.title: Why a 10-minute walk after meals works so well
faqs.summary: Walking gently for 10-15 minutes after lunch and dinner blunts post-meal blood sugar spikes by 15-25%.
faqs.answer: Post-prandial glucose peaks 45-90 minutes after eating. A light stroll right after meals uses that circulating glucose directly in leg muscles and reduces strain on the pancreas.

faqs.title: Safe strength training for diabetes and metabolic syndrome
faqs.summary: Twice-weekly bodyweight or resistance-band exercises (chair squats, wall push-ups) build muscle that burns glucose at rest.
faqs.answer: Muscle tissue is the largest glucose reservoir in the body. Perform 2 sets of 10-12 controlled reps twice a week while exhaling during effort—never hold your breath (Valsalva) if you have high BP.

faqs.title: Pranayama and yoga poses safe for hypertension
faqs.summary: Slow nasal breathing (Anulom Vilom, Bhramari) and Shavasana lower stress hormones and resting blood pressure.
faqs.answer: Avoid forceful breath-holding (kumbhaka) or head-down inversions if BP is >=140/90. Stick to gentle seated pranayama, Shavasana, Setu Bandhasana, and Chair Yoga.

faqs.title: Exercise rules when Stage 2 BP or High CVD risk is flagged
faqs.summary: Do not start vigorous running or heavy weights without a physician checkup; begin with conversational-pace flat walking.
faqs.answer: If your BP is >=140/90 or WHO CVD risk is >=20%, sudden intense exertion can spike blood pressure. Start with 15-20 minutes of flat walking and ask your doctor about a TMT or ECG clearance.

faqs.title: Diabetic foot safety before and after exercise
faqs.summary: Wear cushioned, seamless socks and well-fitted walking shoes; inspect feet daily for blisters or redness.
faqs.answer: Neuropathy can hide minor shoe friction. Check both feet after every walk, keep nails trimmed straight, and never walk barefoot outdoors.

faqs.title: Which hospitals have 24x7 Cath Lab and Cardiac ICU?
faqs.summary: Verified tertiary centers like AIIMS, KEM, PGIMER, CMC Vellore, Apollo, Fortis Escorts, Medanta, Narayana, SCTIMST, and Jupiter provide 24x7 cath lab care.
faqs.answer: In an acute heart attack, door-to-balloon angioplasty within 90 minutes saves heart muscle. Always confirm 24x7 cath lab and emergency triage availability.

faqs.title: Accessing dialysis and CKD care at verified hospitals
faqs.summary: Public and empaneled hospitals (AIIMS, KEM, PGIMER, NIMS, SSKM, Apollo, Medanta, KIMS, DMCH) offer dialysis and nephrology clinics.
faqs.answer: Check whether the hospital has a PMJAY / CGHS desk for subsidized or cashless maintenance hemodialysis and regular eGFR/electrolyte monitoring.

faqs.title: What happens in a hospital Cardiac Rehabilitation program?
faqs.summary: Supervised 8-12 week programs combine ECG-monitored exercise, Indian dietitian counseling, and stress management.
faqs.answer: Cardiac rehab lowers repeat heart events and hospitalizations. Hospitals such as CMC Vellore, Fortis Escorts, Medanta, Kokilaben, Narayana, and SCTIMST run structured rehab clinics.

faqs.title: Government health schemes: PMJAY, CGHS, MJPJAY, Chiranjeevi & Aarogyasri
faqs.summary: Public and empaneled hospitals across states accept Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY), CGHS, MJPJAY (Maharashtra), CMCHIS (Tamil Nadu), Aarogyasri (AP/TS), and Swasthya Sathi (WB).
faqs.answer: Carry your Aadhaar/ABHA ID, scheme card, and prior lab reports to the hospital insurance desk before admission or planned procedures.

faqs.title: What to bring to your cardiology or diabetes OPD visit
faqs.summary: Bring 7-day home BP/sugar logs, all current medicine strips, and recent HbA1c, lipid, and creatinine reports.
faqs.answer: Organized records save repeat blood draws and help your specialist adjust doses safely in one visit.

faqs.title: Hydration rules during exercise in kidney disease vs healthy adults
faqs.summary: Most adults should drink water before and after walks; CKD Stage 3b-5 patients should follow their nephrologist fluid limit.
faqs.answer: If you have normal kidney function, hydrate well especially in Indian summers. If you have advanced CKD or heart failure with fluid restriction, follow your prescribed daily fluid allowance.

faqs.title: How to break sitting time at a desk job
faqs.summary: Stand and walk for 3 minutes every 45 minutes of sitting to prevent post-meal lipid and glucose spikes.
faqs.answer: Even regular gym-goers suffer metabolic slowdown if they sit 8+ hours straight. Pair hourly 3-minute walks with neck/shoulder rolls.

faqs.title: Linking lab reports with your ABHA (ABDM) Health ID
faqs.summary: ABHA lets you store and share digital lab results across AIIMS and verified private hospitals without losing paper copies.
faqs.answer: Ask the hospital ABDM desk or use an ABDM-enabled app to link your ECG, HbA1c, and creatinine history.

faqs.title: Minimum weekly target vs optimal weekly target
faqs.summary: WHO & ICMR recommend at least 150 minutes/week of moderate aerobic activity plus 2 days of muscle strengthening.
faqs.answer: Even 10-minute blocks add up! Consistency 5 days a week matters far more than one exhausting weekend session.

exercises.name: Brisk Walking
exercises.benefits: Improves insulin sensitivity, lowers BP 4-8 mmHg, boosts HDL
exercises.cautions: Use supportive shoes; start 10-15 min if sedentary or high risk

exercises.name: Post-Meal 10-Minute Walk
exercises.benefits: Blunts post-meal glucose spike by 15-25%
exercises.cautions: Keep pace conversational; avoid immediately if dizzy

exercises.name: Conversational-Pace Flat Walking
exercises.benefits: Safe cardiac rehab starter for Stage 2 BP or high CVD risk
exercises.cautions: Stop if chest tightness, dizziness, or unusual breathlessness occurs

exercises.name: Stationary Cycling
exercises.benefits: Low-impact joint-friendly cardio that burns visceral fat
exercises.cautions: Keep resistance light-moderate if BP >=140/90

exercises.name: Outdoor Cycling (Flat)
exercises.benefits: Builds leg endurance and lowers triglycerides
exercises.cautions: Wear helmet; avoid heavy traffic pollution

exercises.name: Swimming (Leisure Laps)
exercises.benefits: Zero joint impact; full-body cardiovascular conditioning
exercises.cautions: Avoid breath-holding underwater if hypertensive

exercises.name: Water Walking / Aqua Aerobics
exercises.benefits: Ideal for knee/joint pain with high BMI
exercises.cautions: Keep water depth chest-level or lower

exercises.name: Badminton (Doubles Recreational)
exercises.benefits: Fun social cardio improving agility and glucose uptake
exercises.cautions: Warm up 5 min; avoid sudden all-out sprints if high CVD risk

exercises.name: Table Tennis
exercises.benefits: Gentle coordination and light aerobic expenditure
exercises.cautions: Stay hydrated

exercises.name: Slow Jogging
exercises.benefits: Strong VO2max and visceral fat reduction
exercises.cautions: Requires medical clearance if BP >=140/90 or WHO CVD >=20%

exercises.name: Stair Climbing (Controlled)
exercises.benefits: High leg muscle glucose uptake
exercises.cautions: Avoid if knee osteoarthritis or uncontrolled hypertension

exercises.name: Elliptical Trainer
exercises.benefits: Smooth low-impact cardio for overweight/obese users

exercises.name: Spot Marching
